Band.BandBiographyText:
Danny Masseling started making music at the age of 16. Beginning with 4-beat programmed loops and breakbeatz etc, his interest in producing music started to grow. It almost became an obession, and in the the same addicitive way as a crack junk smokes his dope, Danny worked on his music day and night. Always searching for improvement and development, his music became more and more professional. What first started out as connecting some loops into a track, slowly turned into serious hardcore house. 

In the beginning of 2001 he decided to send a demo to BZRK Records. The wellknown recordlabel, owned by Mark Vos (Buzz Fuzz). He listened to the demo, and decided he wanted to do serious buzzinezz with Danny. After a while of some mastering and editing, BZRK 33 was born. Under the alias Menace II Society the Son Of A Bitch EP entered the market. Almost at the same time, the first Angerfist EP was released on Overload Records. This was the first time, the name Angerfist appeared in the hardcore scene. Traxx as Criminally insane and Fuck off were immediately recognized as relatively big hits by the public. Danny had set foot in the scene. 

Just a little while later, he released another record, under the name Kid Morbid. This MOH 027 release was also played a lot by DJ's. After this rush of records, his name was pretty wellknown. Now, 2 years later, people know his traxx and appreciate his style. Deep raw kicks, and uplifting melodies stíll punish the eardrumz of partypeople around the world. He is dedicated to keep on making slamming hardcore house...

Band.BandBiographyText:
Endymion was founded in a small town called Wateringen in the Netherlands in 1997.

They made their music using FastTracker and they played at small partiess and local radio stations.

In 1998 they signed a contract with Cardiac Music and they released a string of records on Cardiac's Supreme Intelligence label. People started to call them the Darkcore Xplorers and a new sound was born.

After these initial releases they expanded their studio and started to work with professional equipment.

In 2001 they started their own label Enzyme Records together with Nosferatu under the careful guidance of Cardiac Music. This label is now one of the most popular labels in the hardcore scene.

This little man's mixing skills are very big, ID&T booked this guy many times for their famous Thunderdome Partys. DJ Delirium succesfully produced and still makes hardcore nowadays.

Band.Name: G-Town Madness
Band.BandBiographyText:
The "G" Stands For Their Hometown Groningen (NL).

Richard Jonkman and Eelke Kalberg start producing Hardcore Music in the early nineties. At that time, hardcore and gabber music becomes really popular in Holland and Richard and Eelke feel like they have to be part of it. So do their friends Roel Bakker (DJ Rule) and Rogier Smid. They share the same feeling and also join in. Together they form a group of young enthousiastic producers that, just like many other kids across Hollland, start producing underground hardcore tapes in their hometown Groningen. They use many different names like TNT (Technic Noise Terrorists), The Epitome and finally TND (Technic Noise Demons). The music quality is not top of the bill and their production skills do not meet the highest standards, but they have fun and that is important. They perfom their music with live instruments at school parties and local club houses around Groningen and the first live- acts are born. After a while, Roel leaves the group, but always remains active as a creative member during the live perfomances.

The live- act turns out to be a great way of promoting music and the TND tapes soon become a buzz in the Groningen area. At this point of time, the group's name TND is changed into G-Town Madness. Richard had been using this name when he was still solo and Eelke and agrees that this name really represents their style of music. "G-town" stands for Groningen, the biggest city in the northern part of Holland and "Madness" describes what they bring on stage during a live- act.

Changing the name of the group into G-Town Madness, turns out the be one of the best career moves back then. Now people from Groningen can really relate to their music, cause it represents their city Groningen. As the group becomes more and more popular nationwide, the term "G-Town" is a frequently used term on the streets of Groningen (It still is). A fan base was created.

After many live performances at local clubs and parties in the Groningen area, the time comes to take G-Town Madness to the next level. It is in 1994, that GTM records their first 12": "Dark decades of pain" at Dom records in Utrecht. Their first release means exposure to the rest of hardcore Holland and the boys are really proud that they've finally pulled it off.

But after releasing "Bombs, Guns Blood, Fire", the 2nd 12" at Dom records, the boys make clear they are unhappy with their contract. The record company legally owns the rights of their productions for the next couple of years. GTM realises they have made a "beginners" mistake, by signing a contract without legal assistance

Fortunally, a new and fast growing entertainment company emerges on the hardcore scene. They call themselves Ravers Religion and organize big raves in and around Groningen. They are interested in new talent and want G-Town Madness to become their main act. After negotiations between GTM and Ravers Religion, it becomes clear that this could mean the real breakthrough for the boys. RR agrees to schedule a GTM live performance at every RR party across Holland and in releasing numerous GTM tracks on the RR hardcore labels. It is a dream come true.

Nevertheless, GTM is still signed to DOM records and have their obligations towards them. After GTM and RR threaten to take the record label to court, they finally agree in discontinuing the contract. GTM is free and signs a contract with Ravers Religion.

Ravers Religion turns out to be a big succes. The organization grows fast and so does G-Town Madness. It is 1996/ '97, the Hardcore scene in Holland is getting bigger and bigger. Hardcore dj's become superstars and almost every kid wants to be a gabber. The Hardcore music reaches it's top in terms of popularity and every weekend there are massive raves being organized all over Holland. Trendwatchers estimate that 500.000+ young people are somehow affiliated with Hardcore. Whereas they buy the music or visit the parties. It is big.

The G-Town boys can not believe what happens to them. As Ravers Religion grows, they become more and more popular. They are now the main live- act and perform at almost every RR hardcore party in Holland and abroad. This is really a new experience. RR organizes numerous parties in Italy and GTM perfoms at all of them. Once a month the boys fly to italy to perform at one of the parties there. It is unbelievable.

Not only Ravers Religion is interested in GTM, so are a lot of other promotors. This means that in '97/'98, GTM has like four or five bookings a month. They perform literally everywhere in Holland. GTM is hot and does all the parties. From small clubs to parties like Thunderdome, Rave the city, Hellraiser etc. They perform a lot in Germany, Belgium, Italy and Spain. In Spain, they perform two summers in a row at the famous club "Colossos" in vacation paradise of the world Lloret de mar.

GTM makes some money and they buy equipment for their studio at the RR headquarters in Groningen. They release a lot of records in '97/'98 on many different labels like: Culture shock, Gabberhead and Guilty Records. Gabberhead is a label of the famous XSV company, which had signed artists like Ruffneck. GTM is proud to work for these labels and produces many hits like "silence" and "Determination". All that hard work finally pays off, when XSV gives GTM the opportunity to manage two labels off their own: Madness records and Undercover Mafia Records. They also start a merchandising line with GTM longsleeves and slipmats. It is all to good to be true. GTM also makes a video for the popular hardcore show "Hakeehh" , that is shown on the Music factory. At that time, G-Town Madness uses a lot of aliases like: Damnation, Dj Crossbone and Mad-E-Fact, Hardcore Element vs. Bad news and 1st offence.

Meanwhile GTM makes a lot of friends with fellow dj's and producers. They travel a lot with dj's like Isaac, Petrov and Buzz Fuzz. That is always a lot of fun and always crazy. Richard and Eelke spin as Dj Crossbone and Mad-E-Fact in lots of places All over Europe and Holland.

It's 1998 and G-Town Madness is considered to be one of the top live acts in the Dutch hardcore scene. Together with young dj's and producers like: Isaac, The Viper, Attic and stylzz, Promo and Panic, they are labelled as "the new generation" producers. GTM has a close relationship with Isaac, The Viper and Attic&Styllz. They've become friends for life. In 1998 GTM releases a big party hit with Attic & Styllz: The legacy continues, which is still a much played party track. In that year, G-Town Madness also travels with DJ Isaac to Los Angeles. Not many dj's play over there at that time.

In 1998 the Dutch Hardcore scene is declining. The scene is rapidly getting smaller and hardcore is not as popular as it used to be. Lots of people blame the media for ridiculing the gabber as a drug abusing moran. Others say it's the clashes between soccer Hooligans at parties. Nobody really knows what causes the downfall, but it's a fact that Hardcore scene will never be as before.

The Glory days of hardcore are over. The labels and recordcompanies are falling like domino's, Party promotors are bankrupt and the record sales drop. The gabbers let their hair grow and the once so big hardcore family is nearly a fraction of what it used to be. What will the future bring? No one knows. The consequences for G-Town Madness are catastrophical. They lose their own labels because XSV has gone bankrupt and Ravers Religion quits organizing parties. The foundation they had built together with RR has collapsed. They'll have to think of a whole new plan.

In 1999, G-Town Madness signs a record deal with Combined Forces in Den Haag, one of the few record companies that survived the dowfnall of hardcore. G-Town Madness releases a 12" on Samurai records and does several remixes. There are lesser hardcore parties that year, but GTM still gets bookings for performances. Usually abroad, but also still in Holland. They travel with Isaac to Los Angeles and also perform a lot in Germany.

It seems hardcore is still alive. Some big hardcore parties are packed with people and small time promotors still organize parties.

It's the year 2000 and G-Town Madness just released a new 12" on Dwarf records. It's called "Locked down" and seems to be a serious party hit. Whereas Eelke is getting more bookings as a dj, Richard and Rogier Smid take care of the bookings when he's not available. GTM performs in Switserland and several other places in Germany and Italy. Hardcore is growing abroad it seems.

In Groningen, the hardcore scene hasn't changed that much. G-Town Madness is proud to see a lot of Dj's from Groningen doing their thing. They keep the hardcore vibe alive. Organizations like North Support and Lords of Terror, organize lots of parties in Groningen and manage to create that old "G-Town" party atmosphere. One big family… like it always used to be… It has not really changed... It's just different…

Band.Name: Promo
Band.BandBiographyText:
Sebastian Hoff, also known as Promo, was born on April 12 1976 and started DJ-ing in 1992. Because he didn’t have a resident club, he organized his own events in local clubs. Because of this, he came in contact with well-known names in the hardcore scene.

At the age of 19, Sebastian produced his first track under the alias Section-8 together with Prophet, The that became a hit thanks to the release on Thunderdome IX - The Revenge Of The Mummy. His success continued when he produced a remix of the song “Don't Speak”, which he called “Shut Up!” that was released on the same record (Shut Up! / Born Whappie!) as his remix of “Born Slippy” (Born Slippy) “Born Whappie!”

Although it was a success, he didn’t like the style. The ‘hardcore sound’ of the mid-90’s was to happy, and he missed the strong, and raw sound, which was (in his opinion) the true way hardcore should sound. In 1996 Sebastian, already known as the famous DJ Promo, was contracted by ID&T. Under the ID&T label Sebastian produced over 80 tracks, but his strong, and more raw sound was loved by the hardcore-fans.

In 2000, he decided to leave ID&T so he can do what he want, experiment with the sound of hardcore until he found what he wanted. Without the limits of the record-company. Together with his colleagues of ID&T DJ X-Ess and Catscan the The Third Movement label was born. This was a step forward into the direction he wanted to go. His first releases on his own new label look like statements against ID&T. Running Against The Rules and My Recipe For Disaster even features a spoken message called “Move Forward”. Because of DJ X-Ess and Catscan left The Third Movement 2004 to start there own label, Promo was the man-in-charge of The Third Movement. On the The Third Movement he succeeded in what he wanted, creating his own style and sound, and giving new names the same opportunity. Artist like D-Passion, Peaky Pounder, Tommy Pulse and an other old colleague Dana were given the opportunity to develop there own style. Sebastian’s style is still changing and it will stay changing for a long time.

Band.Name: Hardcoholics
Band.BandBiographyText:
Hardcoholics is hardcore duo ceated in '98 in Marseille and consisting of two artists : DJ LOKY et KYO-O . Their style is no-compromising Hardcore , brutal and dance-floor oriented. 
DJ LOKY comes from the hip-hop scene where he started playing in '95 with a local band and quickly becomes fond of electronic music and computers.

Band.Name: Frazzbass
Band.BandBiographyText:
Milan based, Frazzbass a.k.a. Francesco Adornetto, has been playing all around Europe, in all the biggest events for the last four years. Resident at major european parties like: Hardcore Nation & Undercostruction, Starfuckers, Fuckparade, Dark Park and many others.. (check the old dates)
In the april of 2000 he started to played as name: Milan Speedcore Project live. 
This project was created by him to grow the industrial/speedcore movement in italy. He continued it together eight artists: Rotello, HCM, Schrill, Hotrebor, Fabrikill, Tannoizer, Twilight, Kriminal Terrorist.. For a lot of internal reasons M.S.P is DEAD.
In '99 the speedcore genre was unknown, but with this project, a lot of people apprecieted it in Italy and in rest of Europe.. 
The purchase of Fast Tracker 2 in 1998, provided him with the 
means to experiment with beats and noise himself. 
Influenced by his love for music and driven by the the rage of a young boy, he established his first release on vinyl in 2001. 
He created his label Cerebral Destruction - Shit And Noize Art, to develop quality of noise music in Italy,and continue to grow the movement. 
From 2001 to 2003 he produced a lot of cd's, mix and vinyls (check the discography) and distributed the first five S.A.N.A. (12") by himself during his party dates in europe [over 2500copies!].... but now all s.a.n.a. products are in exclusive to soundbase music in Leipizing - Germany. 
In 2003 He started to collaborate with the precursor of hardcore music in Italy: 
The Stunned Guys. With Rotello made a nice speedcore remix of the famous "Bim Bum Bam" track..
After months of work, in spring 2004 he made the newest double cd compilation, 45 tracks including collaborations with a lot of producers like: Komprex, Splitter, Deadlock, Amiga Shock Force & great extra videos.. Soon new release available 
(check the news in speedcore.it home)
Frazzbass at this time is a reference for alternative music, only Italian DJ/Producer with Komprex & Rotello capable to attract several hundreds of persons for a speedcore/noise live act!
Francesco Adornetto play also other kind of music under other art name's:
Crashdisorder is the name of him, when he play/produce special drum'n'bass, tech'n'bass, or braindance set..
The Geysers (with Hotrebor & Syrob) is a new project darkcore/industrial/frenchcore.
At the same time, he is studing as audio engineer at Sae institute, and starts using synthetizers and samplers: tr909, sh101, juno2, korg's... 
After years of tracker like: FT2, Modplug, Renoise... He is working with Synapse Orion plus plugins & virtual instrument. He starts to use Logic and Pro-tools.

Band.Name: Drokz
Band.BandBiographyText:
My whole life is dedicated to music, but i started taking it on another level in the early 80's as a Hip-Hop DJ/MC in a youth centre. Later on i met Big Mike, who is, 30% of general noise in the army and he connected me with tails in 1990. Acid house was there and house was growing with party's and all that, but the big bang was this thing called "Gabber". 
In 1991 me and a friend called Conabis made a demo in the studio of tails (A.K.A General Noise Studio) witch contains the first track with the title hake, Every exciting label thought it was to hard so we released it ourselves on our own label called 289 records. We released 5 E.P.’s on that label and had a small gabber hit with "Gabber House" from boom terrorism witch we made ourselves, During that period we also made some tracks for Lex Van Coeverden's Dance International Label (Lex is the owner of Cunt records and Producer, believe it or not, of Atlantic ocean's "waterfall"). 
We we're sick and tired of all the paperwork that a label gives you, so we quit the label and focused on making music for dance int. In 1994 General Noise had a gig in the famous Energiehal in Rotterdam and i asked if i could mc on their gig. They said yes cause they know i was a mc in the past. Just a few months after that they signed to ID&T (Thunderdome Party's & CD's ) and i mc-ed at all their gigs (Tails & Noizer live and Noizer as a DJ). 
A few months later ID&T offered me a deal i couldn’t refuse so i signed a contract with the article that i still could make records for Lex, witch i did. Now everything was going crazy.....I did every big and small party's across Holland including some party's with 25.000 people in one hall and the Thunderdome truck on the love parade in 1996, meanwhile i hosted a show called "Hakkeuh" on national TV and I did several guest appearances on TV & TV Talk shows about gabber, I also received a Thunderdome (public chosen) award for best mc in 1997, so you can imagine it was a very crazy period. Later on in 1997 i had a deep conversation with the A&R manager of ID&T about my style of music witch was again...too hard, we split up and I started Cunt Records with Lex, the rest you know. 
The reason i started Cunt Records, is that i wanted to put Holland back on the map with some real hardcore instead of the kiddie gabber.

During the following four years X-ess played at most major parties throughout Europe: Thunderdome, Mysteryland, Energy, Global Hardcore Nation, etc.
In the year 2001 Martijn decided, together with his friend and colleaque Dj Promo, to start his own independent label: The Third Movement.
The label has been focussing rather on creative output then on commercial succes, giving new artists a chance to experiment and test their style.

Band.Name: DJ Daisy
Band.BandBiographyText:
Daisy (her real name) discovered electronic music at a french rave party in 1992. She learned how to mix in 1996 and spun live for the first time the same year at a rave party in Paris, as YSIAD. Passionate about scientific research, she decided to study biology at Paris VI University. 
She passed the first & second year in life sciences with distinction, received a master’s degree & bachelor’s degree of physiology, a postgraduate diploma of psychopathology and she began a Ph.D. in neurogenetics.
In addition to her DJ-activities, she founded the INSOMNIACS association with several friends in 1998 in order to fulfil the need to share her passion.
Promoters of Parisian techno collectives noticed her during live mix sets and proposed residencies for Process and Exist parties, besides her Insomniacs residence. She plays in Paris frequently but also in many other French cities (Bordeaux, Lyon, Dijon, Montpellier, Lille, Strasbourg, Perpignan…) and has played in several European countries (Belgium, Spain, Germany, Holland…).
In 2001 she went into partnership with A. Kahn and composed her first record as MANDRAGORE. Three records were then released in 2002 on Mirage, Gazole and B.E.A.S.T. Records.
In september 2002 she received a Ph.D. in neurogenetics with the highest level of distinction and she decided to devote herself entirely to her other passion: electronic music.
In 2003 her first mix CD was released on Human-UWe and Daisy joined the booking agency of the famous dutch label: The Third Movement. That same year she performed live at several big european events such as Mysteryland (Haarlem). Her second mix CD (r_AW Essential Mix 01) is released on The Third Movement in april 2004. At least five records are planned to be released during 2004 on french and foreign labels. Her track "Kiss Me", released on EBE Company, is in the 2nd Gen Thunderdome CD tracklist. Daisy officially joins the Third Movement crew and becomes a "Third Movement artist".
Musical styles: Techno, Hard Techno and Hardcore 
Her performance is a joy to look at and listen to, due to her enthousiastic appearance and her special touch which combines a dancefloor spirit with a dark atmosphere, huge kicks and groovy hi-hats, precise mixing with lively cuts and speeds ranging from 130 (Techno) to 180 BPM (Hardcore).

Band.Name: Digital Boy
Band.BandBiographyText:
Once upon a time there was a Technological prodigy of sound that crashed upon the Italian music scene like a title wave. Luca Pretolesi ascends on the world of music as Digital Boy in 1990. He brought with him a new sound which was dynamic and cutting edge like no other on the Italian dance floors, a sound known as techno. Like a fever without vaccine Digital Boy's debut record entitled “Kokko” sold over 10,000 units in the first week of release. This was done in a country smaller than the size of California. Digital Boy became a house hold name on every radio station and dance club; as people danced to his beats and paraded to his sounds. 

Digital Boy would make Flying Records his home in the nineties; along with other artist such as, De la soul, Digital Underground, House of Pain, Paris, Molella, Massive Attack, Interactive and Human Resource, just to name a few. He also went on to share the stage with Adamski and Seal, Moby, Carl Cox, West Bam, Dr Motte, Jeff Mills, Doc Martin, Lenny Dee, and Frankie Bones, touring the world and spreading his sound. This was also the year of his first album “Technologiko” from which two hit singles were extracted; “Gimme a Fat Beat” and “OK Alright”. To insure his place with the dance producing elite such as Black Box, Speedy J, Mauro Picotto, LA Style and the likes, Digital Boy went on to release a double album “Futuristik” with yet another two hit singles. The third album released by Digital Boy had a single that would take him to the highest position in the national sales charts as he sat at number one for 7 weeks.  

His name and face appeared in DJ Magazine, Mix Mag, Raveline, Urb and Discotec along with numerous others published in the USA, Germany, Holland, Italy, France and the UK.  His popularity was compounded by public appearances as both live performer and DJ in locations such as; Cocorico (Riccione, Italy), Number One(Brescia, Italy), Studio 54 and Tabu'(Las Vegas), Gheodrome (Rimini, Italy), Parkzicht (Rotterdam, The Netherlands), Fubar (Glasgow, UK), Limelight (New York, USA), Kaboom (Chicago, USA), Lizard Lounge (Dallas, USA), and The Love Parade in Germany. He was a headliner at the biggest Rave events the world had ever seen such as, Thunderdome, Rezerection, Evolution, Extreme Invasion and many others in Holland, England, Scotland, Ireland, Italy, Mexico City and Switzerland not to mention one of the first Rave events to unite over 6000 techno fans in Los Angeles,USA. 

Truly a godfather of “Electronica” Digital Boy currently continues spreading the sounds of dance and party with a flare for the unique. This 12 year veteran delivers beats with technical finesse and creative vigor like so few others.

Band.Name: Ralphie B
Band.BandBiographyText:
Ralph was born on 6 april 1977 in Zwijndrecht, Holland. Today he is living together with “Dian” his girlfriend in Hendrik Ido Ambacht, a small city near Rotterdam. From child age he has been into music. Always have been playing around with keyboards, tapedecks and later tracking programs on the PC. In 1997 he bought his first synth and started working in midi. The style he made was melodic and trancy, influenced by Low Spirit, Fire and Bonzai Records. 

In 1999 his tracks were discovered by AMP (former 80 AUM Records, wellknown for the classic Human Resource - Dominator) after sending in a demo CDR.
A few months later his first record “Alpha Breed - Beyond the Moon” came out on Deal Records (Combined Forces) and it did great. It was played by DJ Jean and so it appeared on many compilations. The next record “Epic Future” was released in January 2000 and had even more success. More “Alpha Breed” releases and remixes followed on Deal Records and Impetious (Warner Music). 

In the beginning of 2001 Ralph created a track which was a bit different from the Alpha Breed style. (Less cheesy !!). The track was noticed by Blackhole Recordings, home of DJ Tiesto and it was released in July 2001 as “Ralphie B – Massive” on “Trance We Trust”. The track became a huge success. It was slammed by all the big jocks: Tiesto, Paul van Dyk, Judge Jules, Armin van Buuren, Ferry Corsten etcetera. Massive got signed to Paul van Dyks Vandit Records (GE) and to Ministrys Data Records (UK) including some cool remixes of Mirco de Govia and Filterheads. It appeared on many big compilations. Ralphie B-Remixes followed for Dario G., Tastexperience, Dance Nation and Misja Helsloot. 

A project with a somewhat harder, tribal style was finished and released summer 2002 as “Midway - Monkey Forest” on In Trance We Trust. With success. Slammed again by all the big djs and signed to Lost Language (Hooj) released in march 2003 including remixes. Ralphie focussed on his Midway guise and released another record in march 2003: Midway – Inca. This track was signed to Tiesto’s compilation “Nyana” and played by all the big names. Also, a Midway remix of Solar Stone - Solarcoaster was released on Lost Language with a lot of success. The story continues as we speak: more releases and remixes will follow in the following months of 2003. 

Since producing always has been a hobby to Ralph he not take the step to become a fulltime producer yet. In daytime Ralph is a ICT Engineer, at night time and weekends he turns into a producer. Ralphie is no DJ, but who knows what the future will bring… [Generated by DBX]

He has after that had releases thru labels like Merck (Miami,US), Rikos Records (Finland), Surgery Records (Australia), Neferiu Records (Canada), Autumn Records (US), U-cover (Belgium) and Zeal Records (Belgium).

Band.Name: Orkidea
Band.BandBiographyText:
Orkidea has been voted Scandinavia's Best DJ twice in Danish Megamind's voting and elected five times as Best DJ at Finnish Club Awards.

He's been Renaissance Worldwide Helsinki resident and has played all around the world in Berlin (Tresor, WMF), Ibiza (Pacha), Hong Kong, France, UK, Denmark (Roskilde Festival), Tokyo (CODE), Toronto (Wintergalactic), Egypt, Macedonia, Russia (Tunnel Club), Frankfurt (Nature One Festival) and Amsterdam (Panama). At these events Orkidea has played with Paul van Dyk, Tiesto, Sven Väth, Jose Padilla, Chemical Brothers and The Prodigy just to name a few.

In 1999 Orkidea released his track "Unity" on Steelfish Records UK. It was played by all the big names including Pete Tong and John Digweed and was played by both Sasha and Paul Oakenfold as opening track for their Essential Mix on BBC Radio 1. Since then he has released various singles on Five AM, Black Hole, Unity and Sential Records. Orkidea has also released two albums and one mix CD on Universal Music. The releases have earned many chart positions including Finnish singles chart #1 in 2005.

Orkidea has made remixes for legendary dance labels like Nettwerk (DJ Tiesto: Flight 643), Vandit (Aalto: Rush), Hooj Choons (Space Manoeuvres: Stage One), Lost Language (Tilt's 12), Solaris (Way Out West: Killa) and remixed mainstream artists such as The Doors and Bomfunk MC's. His work has been included on Renaissance, Gatecrasher, State of Trance and Ministry of Sound CD compilations.

He (rather inactively) runs his own Unity Records with artists like Slusnik Luna, Beatpusher and Dallas Superstars. In 2009 he joined Andy Moor's AVA Recordings label as A&R. He has also written and produced score music for three films and various TV-ads.

As a DJ Orkidea is a real chameleon. His sets can be anything from classic to progressive house, trance, breakbeat, minimal, techno and psy, all depending on where and with who he is playing and the theme of the party. He holds the record of playing the longest ever DJ set in the history of Finland after spinning non stop for a whopping 23 hours on January 1st 2010 at club Red Rum in Helsinki. 23 Hours is also the longest possible set any DJ can play legally in Finland since all clubs and bars are required by law to be closed between 4 and 5 AM.

He has been running his own monthly show "Radio Unity" on Finnish National Radio 1 since 1998. After a year of absence he restarted his show in January of 2009 on AH.fm webradio and as a podcast. After a few months the show got picked up by Finnish radio station NRJ as well.

Band.Name: Menno de Jong
Band.BandBiographyText:
Falling in love with music at a very young age laid a firm foundation for Menno's future in the music business. He bought his first trance oriented albums around the age of 8, and at the time was already well on his way in playing musical instruments, as he often hammered away on his father's synthesizer and guitar. A few years after, at the age of 10, he began training in classical piano... but changed to modern music with various influences not much later.

Playing music to other people is something that ment a lot to Menno in his younger days already. This eventuelly led to him appearing behind the dj desk at his own, and other people's parties. After spinning at a school party at club Downunder in Eindhoven, where he lived at the time, he was asked by the manager to become resident Dj on Thursdays and Sundays, where he spun on and off the following 2 years. 

In the meantime he discovered that making music was not limited by what he could play on a keyboard. The legendary fasttracker program opened up a whole new perspective to his musical ambitions, his rather diverse taste in music (ranging from classical to dance) was now proving essential in the sounds he was experimenting with. After several years of on and off experimenting with the sample based programme, he found a more challening medium called Propellerheads Rebirth. After toying with that for a while he discovered a production tool offered by the same company called Reason. This programme took his creative inspiration to the limit, and after about a year of practice, the track Millionfold was produced, which received a tremendous amount of positive feedback from all who heard it.

DJing also took more serious turns. After organizing some underground trance parties in the area, Menno finally started to play at some bigger events, captivating audiences with his beautiful progressive, trance and tech'trance sounds... leaving no one unimpressed by his awesome dj performances. This resulted in bookings alongside some of the biggest names (Don Diablo, Ton TB, Erick E, Six4Eight, Jav D and others), in some of the most incredible venues all over the world (Dream Nightclub, Washington DC (USA); Home Nightclub, Washington DC (USA), Club <<O>> in Arnhem (NL), Club 1223, Washington DC (USA), etc. etc.)

Producing wise he certainly did not sit still in the time passing, intensively expanding his studio setup and learning to master the new gear and tools acquired. Eventually he produced the track called Guanxi, which was signed to Anjunabeats several months later, to be remixed by top trance producer Super8. Not long after the signing of that track, Millionfold was signed to Gesture Music, with a remix in the making by Markus Schulz.

Band.Name: Anita Kelsey
Band.BandBiographyText:
Anita Kelsey burst onto the dance scene with style in 1997 winning the UK’s coveted MOBO award for her first album with Sunship, an album on which her vocals were described by ‘The Face’ magazine as ‘soulful and rich’. The second album yielded the massive club hit ‘Try Me Out’ (another Kelsey vocal & co-write) which was an Agia Napa anthem of 2001 and marked Sunship out as one of the UK’s seminal garage acts – culminating in their mix of ‘You Bring Me Flowers’ reaching #1 in the UK national charts. 

Further commercial success came a year later for Anita’s collaboration on D*Note’s Shed My Skin which steamed into the UK & US dance charts,  finally topping the Belgian charts at # 1. The track entered the Belgian national charts, staying for 22 weeks and peaking at # 4 & has so far been featured on more than 30 compilations worldwide. 

Other collaborations followed hot on the heels of this, including the track Clouds with Grammy nominees The Latin Project, Signum, who describe their track with Anita, Come Around Again, as ‘the track we’ve always wanted to make’, rising Black Hole star Cor Fijneman with Healing, new Bluefish collaboration (Evolution) with ' Been Too Long'and future releases pending with UK &  worldwide producers such as Will Bruner (PMT), Innate, Meat Katie, Rui da Silva, Matt Darey, Robbie Rivera and many others.

Anita is also approached on a regular basis by labels and producers to write for other artists such as recent Virgin signing ‘Lost Witness’ whose first two singles are co -written by Anita and performed by Tiff Lacey who sang on Paul Oakenfold’s Hypnotise.

Her own project Toyshop formed with David Sun has also been gaining recognition with their recent single Million Miles being voted Top Tune in IDJ Magazine and gaining support from prominent DJ’s such as Pete Tong, Pete Heller, Timo Maas and others. It has also been included on Defected’s Café Mambo 10th Anniversary compilation with a dub mix by Grammy nominees Bill Hamel and Barry Jamieson.

Mark's sound is fresh and energetic. His style ranges from blistering hard trance to full on epic trance anthems. Operating under a number of alias's Mark is a diverse producer that manages to effortlessly switch form one style to the next. As EUPHIONIC Mark concentrates on the more mainstream euphoric edge to his sound and has produced a number of vocal projects with Lisa Abbot. His MUZIKMAN releases are an outlet for his more experimental projects. While as MARCOS he produces tracks for techie harder end of the trance spectrum. He has proven himself as capable of crafting commercial edged trance anthems as he banging out twisted hard stompers.

Spearheading the new wave of UK hard trance producers, MARCOS aka Mark Dearden has literally exploded on to the scene over the last two years. At only 21 he has produced a staggering number of high quality anthems! Working closely with Jay K Walker for a number of years it was inevitable the two would eventually produce a track together. In April 2003 they released 'NIGHTFINDER' EP. Mark's career to date has charted a meteoric rise from bedroom producer to highly respected craftsmen of techie driving anthems. The next logical step is to build Mark's career as a DJ and performing artist. Already a talented DJ (if not sorely under exposed) and an ever increasing international interest directed at his record company for bookings with a little more exposure Mark has the potential to become one of the trance scene's biggest stars. She has released several successful singles and albums, and has toured the world, headlining some of the biggest trance events.

Jan is a passionate and charismatic performer, with a unique ability to connect with her fans. She is one of the most popular trance vocalists of all time, and her music continues to inspire and move people all over the world.

Band.Name: Mateo Murphy
Band.BandBiographyText:
Mateo found his calling at the age of 14, when, looking for an album by a favorite artist, he stumbled onto the 12" section of his local record store. Intrigued by the concept of the remix, he started buying 12"s by his favorite pop artists, gradually moving towards the more underground house sounds coming out of Detroit and Chicago.

Once in college, however, he discovered Montreal's fledgling rave scene, and the harder European sounds that drove it: dropping out of school shortly after, he devoted himself to deejaying full time. After just a few months of intense practice, he got his professional rave debut in 1994, and quickly grew a strong following in Montreal and the surrounding area. Combining the funky rhythms and soul of house music with the hypnotic repetition and intensity of techno, he developed a unique sound that manages to appeal to fans of both. His skill at working a crowd, combined with his impeccable programming and seamlessly mixing, makes his sets irresistible to dance to and has made him one of the most respected DJs in the city. He has held residencies at 5 different clubs in the city (which earned him a top 5 spot in the 'best club dj category' in a recent Montreal Mirror reader's poll), and has made countless guest appearances headlining in bars and raves across the country.

Pushed by the desire to broaden his horizons, he decided that producing his own music was the next step. Fuelled by the local success of his early productions, he decided in 1998 to invest himself fully as a recording artist, cutting down on his hectic deejaying schedule to build up his own studio and produce seriously, developing his sound. The fruits of this labor are quickly coming to light: in a short time, he has released records on all the prominent Montreal-based techno record labels, which has lead to an A & R position at Default recordings, and long-term record deals with several others, including Disktrick and Turbo recordings. His releases consistently find themselves in the charts of some of the biggest DJs in the world, including Paul Oakenfold, Carl Cox, Derrick May, DJ Dan, Josh Wink, and Adam Beyer. And with the increasing demand for his production skills from outside of the city and his growing reputation as both a live act and a DJ, the next year promises to make him one of Montreal's biggest exports. Band.Name: Mutant Disco Police
Band.BandBiographyText:
Anna Jokela, better known as Mutant Disco Police, is a Finnish psytrance artist who started making music in 2004. Born in 1986, she has been a key figure in the Finnish psytrance scene for over a decade. She is known for her unique style of mixing psychedelic trance with disco and funk elements. Her music is often described as being "catchy and upbeat, but with a dark and twisted edge".

Anna first got into electronic music in the early 2000s, when she was introduced to the psytrance scene in her hometown of Helsinki. She was instantly hooked and started attending parties and festivals around Europe.

Over the years, she has released several EPs and albums. She has also played at some of the biggest psytrance festivals in the world, including Boom Festival and Ozora Festival. In recent years, she has also started to branch out into other genres, such as techno and house.

Anna is a skilled DJ and producer, but she is also known for her lively and energetic stage presence. She is always smiling and dancing, and her positive attitude is infectious. Her music is designed to make people dance and have a good time, and that is exactly what she achieves. Whether she is playing to a small club or a massive festival, Anna always puts on a great show.

Each track tells a story, taking listeners on a journey through various emotional landscapes. His commitment to this genre and her unwavering dedication to crafting exceptional music have solidified his position as one of Finland's most exciting Psytrance artists.

Over the years, Psytraumatizer has graced numerous stages across Europe, leaving audiences enraptured by his captivating performances. Her relentless drive for innovation and his ability to push the boundaries of traditional Psytrance have made him a respected figure within the scene.

Looking towards the future, Psytraumatizer continues to explore new sonic territories, eager to share his creations with the world. Band.Name: La Rush
Band.BandBiographyText:
LA RUSH is Lennie Andersson in cooperation with Sandra Oldenstam.

Lennie Andersson aka LA Rush was born in Gothenburg, Sweden, and produces mainly a mix of discohouse, electrohouse, melodictrance, dance & clubmusic. 

Since the beginning of the nineties when the first dancemusic was established in Sweden he felt that he wanted to be a part of the electronic industry/music scene. 
With no means to make his own productions yet he started off 1994 as a dj at his own high school. A few years later his dream of writing and producing his very own dancetunes became a reality. 

Shortly after that he started getting attention from dj..s wishing to play his dancetunes. Around this time he changed his name from Beatloop to LA Rush from the fact that friends called him L.A. 
At the age of 19 he got the opportunity to play at some bigger events and two of his songs ”Around The World” and ”I Love You” where played at a local radio station. 

Between 1999-2002 he started studying music and television production, an education which further helped him develope his skills. This gave him the opportunity to work behind the camera at tv shows which were broadcasted on Swedish television. 

Since 2005 he’s had the privilege to remix songs for artists like Pandora [swe], Richi M [swe], Dj Encore [dk], Dance Nation [nl], Bosson [swe], Agnes [swe], Pleasure Center [us], Kelly Pepper [uk] to name a few. 

In 2008 he began a collaboration with singer/songwriter Sandra Oldenstam and right now they are writing and recording their debut album ”Feel The Rush”. 
The first single will be the uplifting discohouse tune "Call My Name" with a release date in the fall 2009.

Band.Name: Richi M
Band.BandBiographyText:
Richi M (real name: Richard Moldovan) was born on March 22, 1974 in Hungary. In 1980, his family and he came to Sweden for vacation. They met a friend who spoke warm about Sweden. His father thought that they will have a better future in there and decided that family should stay. When he was seven, his father, a drummer back in Hungary, gave him first keyboard. Richi M started with one key, then three, then chords and finally started writing his own songs.

At youth age Richi M was more interested in sport than in music. He did play tennis, lifted weights and did some gymnastics as well, however in the end, music won!

When he wrote his first songs, he showed them to his friends. They liked them very much. As a matter of fact they told Richi M to find a label, which he did and Fluid Records got interested. At that time he also met two guys:Anders Erikkson and Fredrik Johansson from group EARTHBOUND. Richi M has been storming the Swedish dance, airplay and retail charts since his first single released back in 1997 called "Perfect World" written by him but produced by EARTHBOUND. This single reached #23 on the retail chart with airplay on all the major National radio stations.

Both Richi M and EARTHBOUND followed ANTILOOP tread. Richi M refers his style to POP-GOA. When he was young he was much into RAVE and discovered how much the modern dance music has given to him. He doesn't want the GOA to be reached only by the blue, red and yellow haired kids, but also to people who listen to artists like E-TYPE. He is trying to mix nice POP synths with GOA to make it easier to listen to, but at the same time wants to do it in a mystical way.

His second single "One Life To Live" was one of the 25 most played songs on Swedish radio when it was released and was the second highest new entry on the retail chart at # 15 (reached # 14 in Finland). It peaked at #9 on the Dance chart. The single has been a favourite at London's house and epic house clubs, as well. as the renowned club Cream in Liverpool and has received airplay on the London radlo station KISS FM and on Graham Gold's BBC radio show. "One Life To Live" was remixed by Johan S, who also, did the remix of Beastie Boys' "Hold It Now Hit It". The track was one of the most played at the club "Manu Nlission" (at the Ku Discoteque) in Ibiza. Johan S has also remixed Richi M third single "Wake Me Up" which reached Top 20 on the retail chart.

His first album Perfect World was released in July of 1998 and peaked at #14. Richi M's fourth single "12th Planet" taken from this album was released in Autumn of 1998. The video for this single was among "The Most Played Non-Playlist Videos" on MTV Nordic for several weeks.

Richi M was nominated for a 1998 Grammy Award in Sweden for his much awaited album Perfect World in the category "Modern Dance".

Richi M has evolved. more into epic house and Ibiza. He also works as a DJ, as which he plays more progressive, house and trance. He has played. both in Sweden and England. Currenty he is not only an artist, writer and DJ but also became a sought producer and remixer. His current work is the remix he done for another Scandinavian Artist Van

Richi M currently lives in third largest Swedish city: Göteborg. He likes "AIKIDO", a Japanese self-defense sport where kicks and hits are not allowed. His taste of music falls more into soft and relaxing sound. No wonder why he likes artists like Mike Oldfield, Yanni, Enigma or Enya. When time permits Richi M watches Discovery Channel, new programs and movies. He is particulary interested in documentaries related to UFO. (actual as 2001)

Deepwide is an electronic dance music project from Turku, Finland. It was founded in 2003, and is a collaboration by Matti Järvinen and Tommi Hatakka. Matti and Tommi have been friends since kindergarten and work closely together on Deepwide.

Their interest in electronic music began in the late 90s, after having been introduced to tracks from acts such as Gouryella and System F. As this interest grew, they were eventually encouraged to start producing by themselves. Although they started producing independently at first, the friends soon found that they could work well together, complementing each other musically.

Uplifting sounds, melancholy melodies and groovy rhythms are the central aspects of the Deepwide style.

Band.Name: DJ Dazzle
Band.BandBiographyText:
DJ Dazzle was born January 25th 1977. At the age of fifteen he visited the local club Spock in Breda, The Netherlands and heard DJ Tiësto for the first time. He was hooked on dance music. He bought his own turntables and mixer and started to play at student parties with his own gear. 

Two years after he became a resident DJ at The Spock, Dazzle started out at Black-Hole recordings with the Freedom mix compilation series. After the success of the first Freedom, three sequels followed. DJ Dazzle also released Soundbox, a 2CD. All mixes are documents of Dazzle's excellent taste and superb mixing skills and were released on Black Hole’s sub label Songbird, where the Tiesto series In Search of Sunrise is also released on. From the first Freedom on, his sound has developed into the style of music that he plays at his gigs nowadays, rhythmic and energetic tech-trance and tech-house. Also he likes to play the harder types of trance and progressive. 

DJ Dazzle also produces his own tracks, and has worked together with other artists such as Cor Fijneman, Misja Helsloot, Erik de Koning (Three Drives) and Geert Huinink. He remixed artists as Way Out West, 2Souls, Q-lock, Andain and Vank. 

Nowadays Dazzle is booked all over the world and has played from Mexico city to Oslo and from Tel Aviv to Miami. Some venues and events he has played in The Netherlands in 2005 are Melkweg, Panama, Off Corso, Power Zone, Hemkade, Nighttown, Fast Forward Dance Parade, City Lido, Matrixx, Nightlive, Kingdom Venue, Hollywood Music Hall, Impulz, Extrema Outdoor and Dance Valley.

Band.Name: DNS Project
Band.BandBiographyText:
Rene Pais, more known as Clashback and DNS Project, was born on the 25th of March, 1988 in a small Estonian town called Parnu. His interest in music started at the age of 7, when he started to take piano classes. After getting his first entry-level gear in summer of 2004, he started to produce his own first tracks. It took a while to acquire all the basic producing skills. 

In the spring of 2007, Baroque Records released his very first tracks. His first notable track ‘Invisible Touch’ was signed by FiveAM Records right away next. This track was pretty outstanding from the previous ones: electro, tech and trance put together into one piece. In addition to the Original mix, another producer ‘Beat Service’ from Estonia, made a really good remix of it. The track was released on FiveAM’s new techy sublabel called ‘FlutterSpark’ and gained huge support after the promotion. It got played by names like Tiesto, Marco V, Carl Cox and many many others. In DJMag, the remix was reviewed as ‘dancefloor smasher’ hit. ‘Invisible Touch’ also reached position #2 in one of the Baltic States biggest dance music radio station POWER Hit Radio’s 2007 year top40 chart (listeners vote). Right away after, DNS Project and Beat Service made a collaboration ‘Polymental’. They remixed several FiveAM Records artists before their first smash single ‘Chapter One’. The Mark Sherry’s remix of this track was considered to be the one of the biggest techtrance productions of the year 2008. It got played by most of the top trance names out there. After several live and radioshow plays by Armin van Buuren (Armin Only events, ASOT, Mixmag CD) and Tiesto, ‘Chapter One’ also reached A State of Trance Yearmix compilation of 2008. Meanwhile, DNS Project released several productions under his uplifting ‘Whiteglow’ alias as well, with one of them called ‘Airbourne’. This track got supported by all the top names out there. DJ Tiesto played it on almost every gig in 2008, also featured it on his "Top 20 of 2008" mix. In 2009 Rene signed several progressive-trance tracks to Armada Music, under the Lens Flare alias. 

2010 was a BIG year for Rene. Vocal trance tracks like "Mindful" and "Timestep" got played by the biggest names out there, including Armin van Buuren. In addition for being played 4 weeks in row on the ASOT show, the Ronski Speed remix of "Mindful" was even one of the most played live tracks of Armin in 2010. It also made it to the A State of Trance Yearmix 2010 CD compilation. Armada Music also produced an official video for this track. Remixes for artists like Andy Moor, Mike Foyle, Mark Sixma, George Acosta and Mr Pit were just few to point out. 2011 promises to be a big year aswell. Rene also launched a Clashback sideproject alias, for progressive house tracks. First Clashback release "Outset" (including remix by Michael Woods) was supported by the top names out there, including DJ Tiesto, David Guetta, Markus Schulz, Calvin Harris and Hardwell, to name a few. Many new tracks and remixes are constantly under production, so keep an eye on this rising talent! [Generated by DBX]

In 2001 involved into syahrani album called Magma as a song writer arranger, programmer, synthesizer, guitarist and composer.
Start his career as a producer in 2003 with a industrial recycle bin project Bukan Dewa and released in 2004 cooperate with TNT records.

In October 2005, INNERLIGHT has succeeded the national music industry when his single Waiting for Nothing was formally contracted by Monster Tunes, the biggest trance label headquartered in England. Two months later, on December 2005
INNERLIGHT started to debut his international career with his trance mix CD Monster Series 001 live in London. In these double-series CDs, INNERLIGHT had the opportunity to showcase his talent by performing in CD 2, where CD 1 was that of Simon Brisky.

In August 2006, INNERLIGHT was the winner of Heineken Thirst Studio which the final event occurred in DJ Embassy Jakarta. As the 2006 winner of Heineken Thirst Studio, INNERLIGHT had the opportunity to perform alongside with BT and DJ Ronin in Heineken?s main event located in Dome Carnaval Ancol on September 8, 2006.
INNERLIGHT also had the opportunity to do a studio session with BT on September 30, 2006 in Singapore. Moreover, INNERLIGHT performed in the Heineken Global Final in Las Vegas, USA on January 2007.

In February 2008, in collaboration with Clubhoppers and Warner Music Indonesia, Innerlight had relased the third album "Clubhoppers Essential Mix #5".The album has sold thousands CD and made many hits track like Moonlight Dreamland, Conversation with You, Going Home and many more.His tracks had been marked as the most anthem tracks by all Indonesia trance lovers.

In international dance music production, Innerlight also has collaborated with many top artist and producer like BT, Simon Brisky, First State, and Tiff Lacey.

He has shared the deck with many popular international DJs such as
Solar Stone, Reece Elliot, Scott Bond, Simon Brisky, Niklas Harding, BT, Gareth Emery, Andy Moor, Matt Darey, First Sate and many others..

Band.Name: Jan Waterman
Band.BandBiographyText:
Born in 1983 and a resident of Breda, The Netherlands. Jan's interest in electronic music emerged during the early nineties when several genres reached its peak in popularity (like euro dance and happy hardcore). In 1999 he developed a serious interest in trance music and started producing under the aliases Son of a Pitch, Yanave and Evanya for labels like [url=http://www.afterglow-records.de]Afterglow[/url], [url=http://www.deepbluerecords.co.uk]Deepblue[/url] and [url=http://www.beatport.com/label/five-am-records/585]FiveAM[/url], gaining support from big names like [url=http://www.arminvanbuuren.com]Armin van Buuren[/url], [url=http://www.ferrycorsten.com]Ferry Corsten[/url] and [url=http://www.solarstone.co.uk]Solarstone[/url].

During the late "zeroes" Jan's musical taste shifted towards hard and melodical electro house. Eventually he got hooked on its new subgenres that are heavily influenced by the intensity and sometimes complexity of dubstep. Since the spring of 2011 Jan has been releasing tracks in these genres on labels like [url=http://www.bigfishrecordings.com]Big Fish[/url] (owned by Canadian producer [url=http://www.lazy-rich.com]Lazy Rich[/url]) and [url=http://www.bigalliance.com]Big Alliance Records[/url]. In the fall of 2011, Jan's sound got noticed by the crew of [url=http://www.bazooka-records.com]Bazooka Records[/url], resulting in that label becoming a "home base" for his new singles, alongside producers like [url=http://www.spencerandhill.com]Spencer & Hill[/url], [url=http://www.fartooloud.com]Far Too Loud[/url] and [url=http://www.electrixx.de]Electrixx[/url].

Band.Name: Kenneth Thomas
Band.BandBiographyText:
Kenneth Thomas has quickly positioned himself as not only one of the top DJs in Detroit he is now becoming one of the most sought after DJs in America. Over the last few years Kt has gone from the headlining resident position on Saturday nights at Motor Detroit (voted number one club in America by URB Magazine, 2001) to headlining numerous events in Miami, Texas, New York, Indianapolis, Chicago, St. Louis and even Toronto's System Sound Bar & The Guvernment. Kenneth has now moved away from local residencies as he is now becoming a national headliner.

With a regular touring schedule in the US and beyond, Kt has now found time to express himself beyond DJing, by bringing his passion for music into the studio. In 2004, working alongside Mike Targanski (Elevation of Markus Schulz presents Elevation- Clear Blue) led to a new series of productions spearheaded by their first release, Elevation & Kenneth Thomas- “Preen” signed to Armin van Buuren’s Armada sub label, Electronic Elements. “Preen” received praise & play from Paul Oakenfold, Nick Warren, D:Fuse  and quickly become a favorite on Markus Schulz’s Global DJ Broadcast. Their second release Varekai has already received heavy play from the likes of Jon O'bir, ATB and Matt Hardwick and was voted Fan Favorite on Above & Beyond’s radio show Trance Around the World. In late 2005 Varekai also reached #2 on the well respected Dutch Dance Charts out of Holland and was the #1 selling Trance track on Beatport.com in April 2006. The summer of 2005 found Kt releasing his first solo productions spearheaded by the track “Tonic” which was picked up by Markus Schulz’s Coldharbour Recordings. Most recently Kt has done remix duties for Oakenfold and Jan Johnston and will soon see the release of his progressive house track, The Orange Room, on Hope Recordings. The Orange Room has already received heavy play from the likes of Steve Lawler, Sasha, Paul van Dyk and Hernan Cattaneo and has been remixed by Nick Warren.

Although busy in the studio, Kt still considers DJing his first love. He programs his set on the fly at every show to match his interpretation of each club and crowd he plays for. His sets can often run the gamut from House and Progressive to Breaks and techno and of course Trance. 

Kenneth’s immaculate attention to detail and his tireless work-ethic have brought him to the attention of many in the industry, including Paul Oakenfold who has signed him to his exclusive Perfecto family and has also tapped Kt to join him on his upcoming North American tours.

Band.Name: Krzysztof Chochlow

First more well-known track, which slowly became a classic of Polish club music, was "We like the House", which is still a crucial part of lots of DJ sets. The track was released as a single and also on a "Beat Traxx" cd (Warner Music).
	In late 2002 Krzysztof Chochlow made a continuation of the first hit "We like the House" - "We like the Techno!". 
	In late 2003/early 2004 he made many remixes of hits such as: Junior Jack - "E Samba" - Latin trip remix (Pool Grooves), In-Grid "I'm folle de toi" - Tribal remix (Pool Grooves), and a little bit earlier - a remix of Snap "Rhythm is a dancer" - Screamin' mix (CD Pool). In 2004 he remixed: "Summer sun" for 4 Strings (Liquid Records), and DJ Tocadisco "Nobody (likes...)" (Superstar Recordings).
	Beginning of 2005, DJKC started making tracks for his first artist CD album named "DJKC Presents vol 1", which was released in June (Pool Grooves). In the same year, DJKC started collaboration with several Polish club music producers, such as: Matys, Sound Players, and foreign, such as: Marc Van Linden, Sandra Flyn, Sundawner oraz Marc Romboy (Marc et Claude - Alphabet City).
	In late 2005 he released his first vinyl labelled as Krzysztof Chochlow - "Release", "Minimal Screw" (Midway Records). The track was played by: Paul van Dyk (No.1 DJ MAG top 100 in 2005), Marc Van Linden (DJ and producer), Eddie halliwell and others, as well as in London radio station BBC Radio 1.

Meanwhile his passion evolved with a deeper and deeper knowledge of music which brought him to subscribe his first techno work in 1992. After that production he worked for many years as a resident dj in various techno-trance clubs, until 1999 when he meets Giuseppe with whom he starts the NU NRG project.

Giuseppe Ottaviani (Born in Viterbo, Italy, 1978): At the age of 7, encouraged by his particular temperament for music he begun to study the piano. In 1995, after developing a fine music sensibility, he became a dj, getting closer through the years to techno-trance music, that revealed itself to be a strong passion. So he began to attend techno parties, at one of which in 1999 he met Andrea, and shortly after started the NU NRG project.

The group has hung up its activity in late 2005. The will to make solo career was the main reason behind this decision. Last releases through Monster Tunes label contain only the old material. Despite releasing some of it recently, there is still a large number of tracks which could be only heard in their live-sets, not anywhere else.

Band.Name: Tilt
Band.BandBiographyText:
Often called 'Mighty' or 'Legendary' TILT have been a huge part of Clubland for 20 years now. They have gone on to DJ and perform in all of the Worlds top clubs and venues, from Ibiza to South America, North America to Australia. The guys have DJ and performed on huge tours supporting Paul Oakenfold, Simply Red and MTV. DJing in super clubs such as Twilo (NYC), Pacha (Ibiza/South America), Space (Ibiza), Amnesia (Ibiza), Womb (Japan), Crobar (Miami), Vinyl (Danny Tenaglia, NYC), Ministry of Sound World tours, Smirnoff Vodka World tours and all the major Festivals such as Creamfields, Homelands and Global Gathering along the way. Mick Park's DJ partnership 'Parks and Wilson' also produced two widely successful Essential Mixes for the Pete Tong show on Radio One (one of which was voted second best of all time behind Sasha & Digweed).


TILT were signed by Paul Oakenfold to Perfecto/Warner Music label, and in 1996 they had their first UK top 40 hit with 'I Dream', more big tracks followed including 'My Spirit' and 'Places'. In 1998 they moved record label to Red Jerry's brilliant Hooj Choons and more hit singles followed. 'Invisible' (featuring the vocal talents of Dom Atkins AKA Grace) was a top twenty hit, and 'Rendezvous' and 'The Seduction Of Orpheus' (a favorite of Danny Tenaglia) were massively influential tracks which moved the progressive/trance-dominated house scene into previously uncharted, darker territory. TILT had become a major force in the international dance music revolution – with their tribal drums, booming bass-lines and unforgettable melodies, they blurred the boundaries between house and trance and supplied millions of dance music lovers worldwide with the soundtrack to their weekend. To date TILT has had seven UK hit singles, and are now registered to the official Chart Encyclopedia in the UK.  Combined together TILT's production & remix portfolio is second to non - U2, Dido, Kasabian, Arctic Monkeys, Paul Van Dyk, Tiesto, DJ Pierre, Laurent Garnier, Inner City, Kevin Saunderson, 'Mad' Mike Banks, Boy George, Paul Oakenfold, Jeff Waynes 'War Of the Worlds', Way Out West, Bedrock, Quivver, Apollo 440, Cosmos. They also collaborated with the late great Malcolm McClaren, Manager of 'The Sex Pistols' on "Lacme - The Bell Song". In 2005 TILT released their debut album 'Explorer' which featured the massive clubland hits 'The World Doesn't Know' and 'Twelve'. Another side project was the New York underground anthem 'West On 27th' by Killahurtz, released on Hooj Choons, it has just been remixed by TILT.
 
In 2011 they produced "No Other Day" which featured Maria Nayler, and re-released the classic "The World Doesn't Know" for Lost Language's 100th release.  If that wasn't enough, 2012 saw the boys hit the ground running with their huge remix of Cosmos "Take Me With You' which was supported by Pete Tong on Radio 1 and Steve Smart on Kiss FM. The band are currently hard at work in the studio, writing and collaborating with various guest artists and finishing off their second untitled album. Its looking really good for the come back kids *men* with DJ support from the legendary Carl Cox, Hernan Cattaneo, Nick Warren, Pete Tong, Armin Van Buuren and Paul Oakenfold plus many other of the Worlds top DJ's. 

TILT have recently played 2 sell-out Live shows at Cream, Liverpool in 2011/12. In 2012 the boys will release brand new material on Blackhole Recordings, Mesmeric Records and Lost Language and have also launched their very own Radio Show 'TILT TV' (Total Volume) on Proton Radio. As well as this they have also started their own imprint club night 'REZ' which they Performed live/DJ at in July 2012 and once again rocked their spiritual home of Liverpool!!

Band.Name: Tritonal
Band.BandBiographyText:
Emerging from relative obscurity in early 2007, in just a few short years Tritonal has become one of the most recognizable names on the modern trance and progressive world stage. Both exceptional talents in their own right, Chad Cisneros and Dave Reed formed a prolific music production partnership from opposite ends of the United States, which exceeded all expectations and proved to be a creative match made in heaven.

The duo met online at a time when Chad was whittling away the hours in his Austin, Texas studio, providing remixes for some of the biggest dance music labels on the planet - Armada, Lost Language, Baroque, AVA Recordings and Alter Ego Records. Meanwhile, Dave was busy in Washington D.C. completing work on his very own artist album. With similar ideas about music production and sound design technique, the pair rapidly formed a close friendship which culminated in Dave packing his belongings and journeying 1,500 miles across country to pursue what now attests to a prosperous collaborative career.

Very few EDM artists today could lay claim to the kind of whirlwind success Tritonal has enjoyed since its inception. Within the very first year of united production, Tritonal’s remixes and original tracks were being pored over and supported by some of the most renowned and respected DJs in the world. Their first smash hit, Piercing Quiet, was voted best track by thousands of listeners to Armin van Buuren’s ‘A State of Trance’ radio show, with subsequent releases such as Daybreak, Lights Over Austin, Suede, Utopia and Kiss Me Here igniting explosive interest within the global trance community, causing chaos in the Beatport dance music charts and receiving significant backing from the likes of Above & Beyond, Markus Schulz, Ferry Corsten, Stoneface & Terminal and Gareth Emery.

Having produced hit after hit at unprecedented break-neck speed, and with a seemingly endless arsenal of fresh sounds and ideas, it’s no surprise that the lads’ more recent releases can be found licensed to colossal label giants Anjunabeats, Armada, Coldharbour, Flashover, Blackhole and AVA Recordings. They have also achieved repute through their tracks being selected for inclusion on a number of sell-out compilation albums, such as Above & Beyond’s Anjunabeats: Volume 6, Markus Schulz’s Armada at Ibiza and Toronto ‘09, Armin van Buuren’s A State of Trance Top 15 and Abbott & Chambers’ Alter Ego Sessions: Volume 2.

With an army of dedicated fans in the U.S, an ever-expanding legion of followers across the globe and a truly memorable, vivacious stage presence which must be seen to be believed, Tritonal shows no signs of a slow-down. Over the past two years, the guys have headlined at clubs and superclubs in Russia, Asia, the U.S, the U.K and Australasia, and have already accepted bookings for some well-known events coming up in 2011. In addition to a hectic production and touring schedule, the pair also produce the ever-popular Air Up There radio show which has provided an ideal platform from which to launch their latest venture – Air Up There Recordings.
"Our vision behind the label is to release emotional, melodic, forward thinking dance music. The heartbeat behind Air Up There Recordings will be to develop intelligent, uplifting trance that has a fresh and evolving flavour. At the essence of every amazing track is a splendid melody or hook, and we will look first for the musical aspect of the tracks we release. Running our own label is something we've always wanted to do and hooking up with Enhanced has been perfect for us!”

Early 2011 also signals the release of Tritonal’s highly anticipated debut artist album. The album will showcase some of their biggest accomplishments to date, alongside some exciting new additions to the boys’ already impressive discography. We certainly look forward to seeing what this dynamic duo has in store for us next!

Suvitus, a dynamic and enigmatic figure in the realm of electronic music, is born under the name Suvi Vaarakallio on September 21, 1985, in Kirkkonummi, Finland. Known for her versatile talents as a DJ, producer, and artist, she has captivated audiences worldwide with her unique fusion of Finnish Psytrance and Suomisaundi.

Under the artistic moniker Suvitus, she presents herself to the world, but her music journey is not confined by this single identity. In the underground scene, she is also recognized by her intriguing aliases: Artistic Nudity and Slutty Surfer. These alternate personas reflect her fearless approach to self-expression, embracing the raw, unapologetic energy that pulses through her music.

Suvitus's journey in music began at an early age, fueled by a passion for the unique sounds of Finnish Psytrance and the experimental spirit of Suomisaundi. Her dedication to mastering these genres has resulted in a distinct sound that is both captivating and thought-provoking.

As she continues to evolve and push boundaries, Suvitus remains committed to preserving the authenticity and integrity of her Finnish roots while simultaneously exploring new sonic territories. Her music serves as a testament to her fearless spirit and unwavering dedication to her craft, making her an influential figure in the electronic music scene.

Band.Name: Alan Parsons
Band.BandBiographyText:
Born: December 20, 1949 in London, England.

Alan Parsons studied a number of musical instruments in childhood but, like many of his peers, settled on the guitar in his early teens. His job in the late '60s at the EMI tape duplication facility allowed him access to many classics of the day, including the tape master of "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band", which fired him to become a recording engineer. He subsequently managed to get work at the Abbey Road studios and participated in the creation of The Beatles albums "Let It Be", "Abbey Road" and the infamous Apple rooftop session. He also went on to work as mix engineer with Paul McCartney and George Harrison after The Beatles split.

Other artists Parsons has worked with include The Hollies, Cockney Rebel, John Miles & Al Stewart but his real ongoing claim to fame was his engineering work on Pink Floyd's "Dark Side Of The Moon" which earned him his first grammy nomination.

It was after this that Parsons co-founded the Project with songwriter Eric Woolfson, creating conceptual albums that featured a revolving cast of uber studio aces and members of bands such as The Hollies, The Zombies & Cockney Rebel. The early albums were inspired by the works of Poe ("Tales Of Mystery & Imagination") and Asimov ("I Robot"), and later by esoteric subjects ("Pyramid", "Eye In The Sky").

During the '90s Parsons expanded his reportoire with a theatre show ("Freudiana"), and a touring live act with long time collaborators, guitarist Ian Bairnson and drummer Stuart Elliott. A long-standing fan of Alan's music, Mike Myers as Austin Powers in "The Spy Who Shagged Me" decided to name his Dr. Evil character's death ray "The Alan Parsons Project". Yeah, baby yeah!!

Alan's music is now taking a new contemporary direction into the world of Electronica. His latest album features a number of notables in the genre including The Crystal Method, Shpongle, The Nortec Collective and Uberzone. The album also features a guest appearance by Pink Floyd guitarist David Gilmour. Alan says, "The industry is changing and I feel the need to capture a different kind of audience while still keeping my identity. Electronic music is the fastest growing music category right now and I'm enjoying working with new people and new technology". The album is now available on CD and will be released in DVD formats. The DVD will contain 5.1 surround mixes as well as new visual material.

Alan has written extensively for the Pro-Audio press and is an acknowledged expert in 5.1 Surround Sound recording. He has often lectured at Recording conferences and Schools of Recording and was the keynote speaker at The Audio Engineering Society convention in 1998.

Band.Name: Barry Jamieson
Band.BandBiographyText: Barry Jamieson is an accomplished producer and talented engineer. His career has spanned the better part of two decades and includes Top 40 Hits and a Grammy nomination. Using the moniker Evolution, Barry and his partner (Jon Sutton), began producing a new sound just as dance music was getting off the ground at Shelley’s and the Hacienda in the UK. Signed to the label Deconstruction, Evolution had two Top 40 Singles in the UK pop charts. Barry eventually co-founded the record labels Fluid and Viscous as a platform for innovative production, working with artists John Digweed, Andy Ling and Jimmy van M, Sean Cusick, Sasha, and many more. Barry made the move to the states in 2004. Based in New York, he rekindled a working relationship with Sasha and produced the albums Involver and Fundacion, both of which entered the iTunes dance chart at 1. A prolific artist and collaborator, in the past 2 years he has remixed singles by Britney Spears, New Order and Madonna with studio partner Bill Hamel. The two earned a Grammy nomination for their incredible remix of Seal’s single “Get together”. Barry has also collaborated with Sasha on remix for Depeche Mode, UNKLE, Spooky, Faithless, Grand National, Petter, Ulrich Shnauss, and many more. A desire to score music for film and television has motivated Barry to expand his production credits. In 2005 he wrote music for FilmFour’s nationally distributed television advertisement for Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon. Barry and Sasha produced feature music for the CBS drama CSI: Crime Scene Investigation. They became the first featured artists to score an entire episode with their work on the CSI show titled “4 x 4”. Alongside Sasha, Barry has also co-written music for CSI Miami and CIS NY. A well-rounded artist, engineer and musician Barry Jamieson divides his time between New York and London. He is member of The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers in the USA and the Performing Rights Society in the UK [Generated by DBX]

Band.Name: Carl Craig
Band.BandBiographyText:
Born: 22 May 1969 in Detroit, USA. 

Carl Craig was a key player in Detroit techno's second wave, following the futuristic lead of originators [a=Derrick May] and [a=Juan Atkins], and eventually collaborating with May. He began recording at the turn of the 1990's, using a number of aliases to release innovative ambient, techno, breakbeat and future jazz sounds. 

One such alias, [a=Innerzone Orchestra], issued "[r=37872]" in 1992, the track largely responsible for moving drum 'n' bass away from the sounds of hardcore and ragga. He later reconvened Innerzone Orchestra as a jazz/techno combo, recruiting jazz composer/keyboardist [a=Craig Taborn], former [url=http://www.discogs.com/artist/Sun+Ra]Sun Ra Arkestra[/url] member [a=Francisco Mora Catlett], and [a=Matthew Chicoine] to help him record 1999's album "[r=43817]". 

Matt Chicoine, under alias [a=Recloose], later signed for Craig's own label [url=http://www.discogs.com/label/Planet+E]Planet E Communications[/url], a peerless dance label employing the same eclectic and futuristic ethos that informs his own music. 

With releases under many aliases, including [a=BFC], [a=Psyche], [a=Paperclip People], [a=69], [a=Designer Music] and [a=Innerzone Orchestra]; Carl Craig has more musical personalities than the average electronic artist. As much as his different guises can confuse though, his music is always easily recognized because whatever he does, it retains that certain Craig-ness of sound. A deep commitment to soul mixed with jazz, often including but not exclusively so, a detroit techno sound, has always been the watermark of his music. 

Even when Craig is destroying dance floors with such songs as the classic track "[r=161616]" (or one of the very many versions of it!) there is always a subtleness and attention to detail that separates his music from that of the typical dance music producer. [Generated by DBX]
